statement: Reserpine | In lists: 1, 2, 4, 5 (A); 6 (B) | Main reason: Risk of orthostatic hypotension, bradycardia, syncope, CNS side effects (sedation, depression, cognitive impairment) | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Low initial dose, half of usual dose, taper in and out. P Lower doses (0.05 mg/d) to normal doses (0.25 mg/d) are recommended. M Avoid if CrCl <10 ml/min. M, E | Alternatives: Other antihypertensive drugs, e.g. ACE inhibitors, or other mediation groups depending on comorbidity (exclude PIM). E || Methyldopa | In lists: 1, 4, 5 (A); 6 (B) | Main reason: Risk of orthostatic hypotension, bradycardia, syncope, CNS side effects (sedation, depression, cognitive impairment) | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Low initial dose, half of usual dose, taper in and out. P Suggested initial daily dose is 250 mg of methyldopa with a maximal daily dose of 1000 mg. M CrCl >50 ml/min administer every 8 h; CrCl 10-50 ml/min administer every 8-12 h; CrCl <10 ml/min administer every 12-24 h. E | Alternatives: Other antihypertensive drugs, e.g. ACE inhibitors, or other mediation groups depending on comorbidity (exclude PIM). E || Clonidine | In lists: 1, 3, 4, 5 (A); 6 (B) | Main reason: Risk of orthostatic hypotension, bradycardia, syncope, CNS side effects (sedation, depression, cognitive impairment) | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Lower doses for initial treatment of hypertension; half of usual dose, taper in and out. M, P | Alternatives: Other antihypertensive drugs, e.g. ACE inhibitors, or other medication groups depending on comorbidity (exclude PIM). E || Guanfacine | In lists: 1, 5 (A); 6 (B) | Main reason: Risk of orthostatic hypotension, bradycardia, syncope, CNS side effects (sedation, depression, cognitive impairment) | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Cautious dosing when using guanfacine hydrochloride immediate-release; start dosing at the low end of the range. M | Alternatives: Other antihypertensive drugs, e.g. ACE inhibitors, or other medication groups depending on comorbidity (exclude PIM). E || Moxonidine | In lists: 1, 3 (A); 6 (B) | Main reason: Risk of orthostatic hypotension, bradycardia, syncope, CNS side effects (sedation, depression, cognitive impairment) | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Caution in cases of moderate renal insufficiency (CrCl 30-60 ml/min): maximum doses 0.4 mg/d; avoid if CrCl <30ml/min. M, E | Alternatives: Other antihypertensive drugs, e.g. ACE inhibitors, or other medication groups depending on comorbidity (exclude PIM). E || Rilmenidine | In lists: 1 (A); 6 (B) | Main reason: Risk of orthostatic hypotension, bradycardia, syncope, CNS side effects (sedation, depression, cognitive impairment) | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Reduce dose in cases of renal failure (CrCl <15 ml/min), M, E | Alternatives: Other antihypertensive drugs, e.g. ACE inhibitors, or other medication groups depending on comorbidity (exclude PIM). preambles.text: The aim of the study was to develop a European list of potentially inappropriate medications (PIM) for older people, which can be used for the analysis and comparison of prescribing patterns across European countries and for clinical practice.

preambles.scope: EU(7)-PIM article: dose and alternative suggestions
preambles.text: The PIM list contains suggestions for dose adjustments and therapeutic alternatives. Dose adjustments and drug alternatives suggested by the experts during the Delphi survey were compiled and included in the EU(7)-PIM list, prioritising in each case those made by the higher number of experts. Suggestions were complemented, if necessary, with information available from the other PIM lists and from Micromedex® [[32](http://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4464049/#CR32)], a commercially available database which contains comprehensive information on drug use.

footnotes_and_definitions.text: E: Experts; M: Micromedex ® [32]; P: PRISCUS list [22]; L: Laroche et al (2007) [3]; McL: McLeod et al (1997) [26]; B: Beers list (2012) [18].
Note: if nothing is stated under “Dose adjustment / special considerations of use”, this means that no suggestion was made either by the experts or in Micromedex® .

'In lists' gives the numbered prior PIM lists in which the substance appears, with Category A (precisely this active substance is named as a PIM) or Category B (a PIM only in certain clinical conditions or comorbidities, or not named but covered as a PIM drug class). 'Does not appear as PIM' means the substance was not a PIM in those prior lists; it is still an entry of the EU(7)-PIM list and is not an exclusion. Entries the panel judged questionable carry footnote d.
footnotes_and_definitions.source: EU(7)-PIM ESM1 legend (footnotes a and d)
